# Inspect Ranges

Inspect Ranges is an [Inspect AI](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk) extension for evaluating models and agents on multi-host cyber ranges. The goal is support for a wide variety of complex networks while still preserving ease of development and deployment:

1.  Ranges are defined in a strict, validated YAML spec (`range.yaml`) covering networks, routers and their ACLs, hosts, attacker foothold, dynamic range generation, defenders, and attack-path definitions.

2.  Ranges run as libvirt/KVM virtual machines orchestrated by an unprivileged container, on any Linux host with KVM (bare metal, or cloud instances with nested virtualization). Windows guests are supported, including Active Directory networks.

3.  Range control runs over the virtio-vsock hypervisor channel, not a network, so nothing in-range can discover, firewall, or connect to the control plane or the agent. The agent runs inside its own VM, contained by KVM and an outer unprivileged container.

4.  For scoring integrity, evidence (pcaps, consoles, artifacts) streams off-instance as it is generated: in-range defenders see only what the agent transmits, while the scoring oracle sees everything.

5.  The design emphasizes speed: a complete eval against a multi-VM range boots, solves, scores, and tears down in about 15 seconds. Windows golden images build unattended in ~3 minutes and restore from memory snapshot in ~1.4 seconds.

## Development

the authoring loop: write range.yaml, validate catches errors immediately, render shows the exact generated artifacts before boot; the six translated example ranges as starting points; "runs anywhere Linux+KVM" with doctor as the readiness check. (This section also owns the ~15s iteration-cycle number.)

## Evaluation

### Datasets

this is the natural home of the range/task split, which hasn't had a home anywhere until now: one range serves many tasks, tasks.yaml as example-dataset seeds, samples targeting flags/objectives. Worth stating explicitly since it's a design decision mirroring Inspect's sandbox/task split.

### Agents

solvers drive guests through the standard sandbox() API, including named sandboxes per host; scaffolds work unmodified (binary injection at ~400MB/s covers inspect_swe-style agents); no egress means tooling is baked or injected.

### Scoring

oracles verified in the environment (exec on targets), evidence off-instance, the defender/oracle asymmetry.

## Architecture

Compilation ends up carrying the single-source-of-truth proof, Control Plane ends on the not-a-network property that Security Model picks up.
